Ternyata pintar secara akademis belum tentu selalu tepat dalam melihat realitas.

Kadang yang dipertanyakan bukan seberapa tinggi pendidikannya, tapi seberapa dalam seseorang memahami keadaan orang lain.

Ketika sebagian orang bisa “menjauh dari bad news” karena punya pilihan, ada orang lain yang justru hidupnya menjadi bagian dari bad news itu sendiri.

Jadi jangan sampai istilah mindfulness berubah menjadi alasan untuk kehilangan kepekaan. Karena kecerdasan bukan cuma soal gelar, kemampuan berpikir, atau sederet prestasi—tetapi juga soal tahu kapan harus bicara, kapan harus diam, dan kapan harus melihat penderitaan orang lain dari sudut pandang mereka.

Pintar itu bukan sekadar tahu banyak. Cerdas itu ketika pengetahuan yang kita punya membuat kita semakin peka, bukan semakin jauh dari realitas.

author: thecritique911
comment_text:
Dear Maudy,
It is quite DISAPPOINTING to see someone with an Oxford PPE background framing the painful realities of this country primarily as “bad news.” PPE is supposed to train you to understand society through philosophy, politics, economics, and public policy—not merely to manage your personal discomfort when confronted with its consequences.
When Indonesians are dealing with fuel shortages, forest fires, food-safety concerns, disasters, and problematic public programs, these are not simply “bad news” that people can mute, filter, or step away from. For many Indonesians, they are not news. They are their everyday reality—their livelihood, their health, their families, and sometimes their survival.
This is where I think your interpretation of mindfulness misses something important. Mindfulness should not become a comfortable distance from reality. Mindfulness also means being present with uncomfortable realities, acknowledging them, and understanding whose lives are being affected. You may have the privilege to step away from the news; many Indonesians do not. Even their “noise” on social media that you called "bad news" may be the only way they can make themselves heard.
And this is where your platform matters.
No one expects you to fix Indonesia. You are absolutely okay to build your own career, create content, or run a skincare business (which ridiculously, one of the sources is taken from Kalimantan's Forest). But with an extraordinary education, enormous public visibility, and a platform capable of reaching millions of Indonesian, it is legitimate to ask: Is this really the most meaningful contribution you can make to the country that gave you scholarship? or, what is exactly your privilege ultimately being used for? for the sake of fame? business? personal branding? or whattt?
Sorry, I think your profile as an Oxford and Stanford degree is not more than an impressive line on a résumé. 
What a shame, Maudy!!!
